author: [deleted]
body:
So, my input is based on really rushing to get to end game. If you are wanting to push up into the top in the shortest amount of time, you want to focus in the classes that make grinding the easiest.

For me, the obvious choice was the dragon knight path. It's a pet focus path and offers a fun dual equipment set up. You can use mage or warrior gear, which makes for some interesting set ups.

Once you get to tier 8, you can really start making that path shine. You pick up freyr and crimson gazer, and suddenly your overworld grind is a complete breeze. Nothing stands up against that combo. You carry that over into bahamut and Nidhogg, and now you're destroying boss dungeons in just a few minutes. The grind towards t10 could not be faster.

Once you get towards t10, that's when the real decisions come into play. By that time, you will own most of the t8 classes, and a few t9 classes. You'll need to figure out what play style you prefer for the endgame. Beowulf is the last in the dragon path, but all the t10 classes have dramatically different play styles from their lower tier counterparts. I steered away from Beowulf and switched to Realmshifter.

I had already bought Nyx before I hit t10 because the class is amazing for pvp, and that was my focus at the time. Realmshifter has an interesting style, but you can also ignore it for the most part and still do tons of damage, while boosting dex to avoid damage yourself. The other t10 classes are heavily reliant on their meta, while Realmshifter seems to do just fine regardless.

Then comes the true endgame content so far, The Morrigan. Currently, if you want to run consistent damage against the Morrigan, you basically have to be running the melee classes. Gilgamesh is a must have at t10, and most players agree it is simply the best choice at the end. Heretic seems to do fine, but I've never played as one, and the few friends I had that picked it upon release have now picked up Gilgamesh for Morrigan.

Tl;dr version:

Pet classes until t10 and then start really exploring.
